decision.detail: I walk over to the patch console where Rita's already got her mic cable coiled. I set my reel on the little shelf next to her tape spool, the one with the sticky note that says ALMA / TUE / LAST TAKE in her handwriting. I don't unspool it. I don't press play for anyone. I just set it down, next to hers, so it's on the patch. One reel, one take, one window. I step back, pull my bag strap down to my hip, and I'm already turning for the door. The Rialto's got that old projector hum in the walls and the station line's still lit. I let the door click shut behind me. I'm not going back tonight. The ballroom lights are on and I can see them through the hall window, all gold and stupid, but that's not what I'm here for. That's never what I'm here for. I walk to the parking lot. My truck's still warm. I don't start it yet. I just stand there in the cold, hands in my jacket, and I listen to the hum from the building. Then I start the engine and I go.
decision.intention: The reel was mine to keep. I said so. But Rita's patch is where the daughter will find it, where it's logged, where it doesn't live in a bag under my passenger seat and get lost or get wet or get eaten by a dog. I'm not the archivist. I'm the operator. I took the picture. I'm putting the print where it belongs. And then I'm gone. The lights can be there tomorrow. The ballroom can do its thing. I've got one charged take in the world and it's not going to be the one I kept in a drawer because I was proud of holding it.
decision.words: I don't say anything to Rita. I just set the reel down. She's got her headphones in. She doesn't look up. I don't need her to. I'm already at the door.
